document.title: GUI runs share one machine-wide lock and bench kills hung runs
document.summary: A new `scripts/gui-run.sh` serializes every VitaDeck window and Vita3K run on the machine behind one `mkdir` lock. `scripts/bench.sh` now runs the GUI in its own process group and kills it when no result arrives within `VITADECK_BENCH_TIMEOUT`.
document.why: Concurrent Vita3K benches from several worktrees shared `~/.vitadeck/vita3k` and contaminated each other's results, and a hung Deck App blocked `bench.sh vita3k` for up to an hour because the timeout did not apply to the emulator ([PR #139](source:s1)).

sources.label: PR #139
sources.title: fix(scripts): GUI runs share one machine-wide lock and bench kills hung runs
sources.gist: One machine-wide GUI lock for bench, vita3k.sh and the CMake run target; bench kills the GUI process group on timeout.

sources.label: Claude session · Oct 27
sources.gist: Orchestrator brief: per-machine lock held only around the GUI run, mkdir-based, stale-PID recovery, release on signal; kill Vita3K on result timeout without timeout/gtimeout; update the bench and emulator skills.

groups.title: The GUI lock and process-group helper
groups.why: Every GUI launcher needs the same lock and the same way to stop what it started ([brief](source:s2)).
groups.summary: `gui_lock` takes the `mkdir` lock that `gui_cleanup` releases on exit, and `gui_start`/`gui_stop` run and kill a command as one process group, which `gui_run` combines for callers.
lookFor: Race: a waiter reclaims a dead owner's lock only after it wins `mkdir "$GUI_LOCK/reclaim"` and re-reads the same owner, then renames the lock away before deleting it, so a second waiter can neither delete a fresh lock nor leave an ownerless one.
Subtle: a dead owner PID that the OS has reused for another process makes the lock look held; the waiting message prints the owner so a human can remove it.

Subtle: `gui_lock` is a no-op when the owner PID is `$$` or the exported `VITADECK_GUI_LOCK_PID`, so `vita3k.sh launch` under `bench.sh` reuses the parent's lock and `gui_run` then runs Vita3K in the foreground inside the parent's process group.

Subtle: `gui_start` turns on `set -m`, so the GUI gets its own process group and a terminal Ctrl-C reaches only the script; its `INT` trap exits, and the `EXIT` trap stops the group and removes the lock.
`VITADECK_GUI_LOCK` overrides the lock path; it is documented only in the code and exists for tests.
A lock directory without an `owner` file (a holder killed between `mkdir` and writing it) is never reclaimed; every run waits and prints `remove it if nothing holds it`.

groups.title: bench.sh: lock after build, stop on timeout
groups.why: Bench runs collided in the shared emulator home, and a hung Deck App never let Vita3K quit ([PR #139](source:s1)).
groups.summary: `run_host` and `run_vita3k` take the lock after building and before writing the request, then `bench_gui` polls for `result.json` and calls `gui_stop` at the deadline or 10 s after the result.
lookFor: Behavior change: the host target used to fail with `vitadeck failed` on a nonzero exit; now any exit that leaves `result.json` counts as success, as `vita3k` already did.
Subtle: the lock is held until `bench.sh` exits, so the `pnpm bench:report` step also runs under it, a second or two.
`run_host` now does `cd "$ROOT_DIR/out"` in the script's own shell instead of a subshell, so later steps run from `out/`; they all use absolute paths.

groups.title: vita3k.sh and the CMake run target take the lock
groups.why: Interactive Vita3K and host runs also skew timings and share the emulator home ([brief](source:s2)).
groups.summary: `vita3k.sh launch` takes the lock before writing the emulator config and runs Vita3K through `gui_run`, and the CMake host `run` target wraps `./vitadeck` in `scripts/gui-run.sh`.

groups.title: Skills mention the lock and the timeout
groups.why: The bench and emulator skills would otherwise not say that runs wait or that a hung run is killed ([brief](source:s2)).
groups.summary: `vitadeck-bench` says runs wait for the lock and time out with the emulator killed, `vitadeck-emulator` says launching waits for the same lock, and `vitadeck-manual-testing` runs `./vitadeck` through `gui-run.sh`.

commits.subject: fix(scripts): reclaim a stale GUI lock by rename, and require a command
commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body:
rm -rf could fail on a lock another waiter had just put its reclaim dir in, leaving an ownerless lock that
everyone waits on. gui-run.sh with no command now fails instead of exiting 0. The manual-testing skill runs
./vitadeck under the lock.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: fix(scripts): only one waiter reclaims a stale GUI lock
commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body:
Two waiters could both see the dead owner, and the second then removed the lock the first had just taken.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: docs(scripts): keep the vita3k.sh command list together in its usage
commits.author: Máté Molnár

commits.subject: fix(scripts): GUI runs share one machine-wide lock and bench kills hung runs
commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body:
scripts/gui-run.sh holds a mkdir lock in /tmp around every VitaDeck window
or Vita3K run (bench.sh host and vita3k, vita3k.sh run and launch, the
CMake run target), waits while printing the holder, and reclaims a lock
whose owner PID is dead. Builds stay outside the lock.

bench.sh runs the GUI in its own process group and polls for result.json;
at VITADECK_BENCH_TIMEOUT it stops the group (TERM, then KILL after 10 s)
and fails, so a hung Deck App no longer blocks a run in Vita3K.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

A lock directory without an `owner` file (a holder killed between `mkdir` and writing it) is never reclaimed; every run waits and prints `remove it if nothing holds it`.
removed: Race: stale reclaim is read-owner, check PID, `rm -rf`; two waiters reclaiming the same dead lock in the same instant can let the second one delete the lock the first just took.
